subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data custody clarification and next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@meddix.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data custody clarification and next steps

Hi Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the handful of clarifying items we promised to follow up on so you can take this back to your security and infra teams: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary requirement: customer-managed key material for model input storage and audit traces; Meddix cannot have plaintext retention outside their control.
- Network boundary preference: if possible Meddix would prefer a Private VPC deployment, otherwise Dedicated nodes with strict egress controls and keystore residency are acceptable.
- Latency & throughput: production latency target ~150ms p95 for inference; anticipated steady-state qps ~120.

Open clarifying questions / next steps we promised: 
1) Keystore residency: Do you require KMS/HSM physically in your VPC (BYOK with HSM) or is a key-wrapping model with customer-managed keys acceptable?
2) Audit/loging residency: Which audit logs must remain within your account vs can be streamed to a Redshift wire in our prod region for operational debugging?
3) Backup and snapshots: Are encrypted snapshots that never leave your project acceptable if retained in your private bucket?
4) Timeline for procurement & compliance review: can you share the internal date when this security review will be complete?

Attachments: redwood-deployment-comparison.pdf (short matrix: Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC), kms-residency-diagram.png (logical KMS options)

Suggested immediate next step: 30-minute follow-up with your infra/security folks and our Solutions Engineer (Connor) to walk the KMS options and provide a quick mapping to your control model. I can schedule for next week if that works.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@meddix.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: security@meddix.com
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data custody clarification and next steps

Thanks, Rishi — good summary. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Keystore: We need an HSM-backed key in our VPC for encryption at rest of any persisted prompt/response logs. Key-wrapping by Redwood is only acceptable if the root key is controlled by us and never exported.
- Audit logs: All request/response metadata must be retained in our project for 365 days; operational traces that contain PII must not leave our VPC.
- Snapshots: Encrypted EBS-style snapshots stored in our account are preferred.

We would like Connor and Laura to join the follow-up to validate the technical approach. Do you have a short checklist you can run us through? Also, can you confirm whether Dedicated nodes allow keystore mounting in customer VPCs or if that capability is only available for Private deployments?

Cheers,
Priya
Head of Security Ops
Meddix

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data custody clarification and next steps

Priya / Rishi / Connor — thanks for looping me in. Short answers up front: 

- Dedicated nodes: we can offer a customer-managed KMS integration where the root key is under your control and we perform key-wrapping at the host level, but mounting an HSM device directly inside the node is only supported for Private VPC/on-prem. For Dedicated we offer a BYOK model with Cloud KMS or customer KMS endpoints and strict egress rules; we can present an architecture that keeps plaintext out of Redwood's long-term storage.

- Audit logs & retention: we can push request/response metadata to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket using secure, mutually authenticated peering. Files that contain PII can be redacted before export as an interim mitigation. Full in-VPC logging where neither the control plane nor the export pipeline touches Redwood infrastructure requires Private deployment.

- Snapshots/backups: Encrypted snapshots can be stored in the customer's cloud account for both Dedicated (via restricted snapshot pipeline) and Private (native in-account snapshots).

Attached: SOC2-A-stub.pdf (excerpt of our controls), and a short checklist PDF (redwood-deployment-comparison.pdf) that maps requirements to capabilities. Connor — I included the KMS residency diagram (kms-residency-diagram.png) in the attachments for your deck.

Recommended next step: I can run a 30-minute technical call with your infra/security on Tuesday 9/7 at 11am PT to walk options and confirm whether Dedicated with BYOK meets their policy or Private VPC is required. If we get their procurement timeline after that call we can scope a Statement of Work.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
